methodological_rigor.justification: This is a pre-specified exploratory biomarker analysis leveraging the randomized phase III COLUMBUS trial (NCT01909453, n=921) with a large correlative cohort: 666 WES, 514 RNA-seq, 336 baseline ctDNA, and 184 on-treatment ctDNA samples. Methodology is solid (Cox proportional hazards with 95% CIs, K-means clustering with silhouette width, recursive partitioning, xCell cell-type estimation) and limitations are explicitly acknowledged including unmatched normal controls for WES, pooling of COLUMBUS parts 1 and 2 with different encorafenib doses, retrospective nature, and lack of multiplicity correction. The statistical approach is adequate but biomarker cutoffs are data-driven (median splits), multiplicity is explicitly not corrected ('hypothesis-generating'), and the on-treatment ctDNA subgroup (n=184) is underpowered for some comparisons.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The analysis provides actionable insights for BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma: it identifies TMB, cytolytic score, PD-L1, and IFNγ signature as candidate biomarkers of encorafenib+binimetinib benefit; flags PI3K pathway mutations and high ERBB2 expression as resistance markers; and supports ctDNA BRAF V600 clearance as a prognostic/response marker. These findings can directly inform ongoing triplet trials (STARBOARD, PORTSIDE) and patient stratification. Oxford LoE is 2b: a retrospective/exploratory correlative analysis of a single randomized trial, not a prospective biomarker-driven RCT.

reporting_quality.justification: As a biomarker/prognostic study, REMARK is the applicable standard; the manuscript covers the parent trial (NCT01909453), patient selection, assay platforms (Personalis ACE ImmunoID NeXT, GuardantOMNI), endpoint definitions, cutoff derivation (median splits), HRs with 95% CIs, and explicitly states results are hypothesis-generating. Reporting is thorough but some REMARK items (REMARK flow diagram of sample disposition, pre-specification of primary biomarker hypotheses, full confounder adjustment) are only partially addressed. No explicit data availability statement or accession numbers for WES/RNA-seq/ctDNA datasets are visible in the provided text, limiting reproducibility.

novelty_literature.justification: The concept that immune infiltration and TMB correlate with BRAF/MEK inhibitor benefit is not new and the manuscript explicitly cites prior analyses in COMBI-AD (ref 29) and cobimetinib+vemurafenib (ref 30) that reported similar IFNγ and immune signature findings. Novelty lies in the combined scope: the largest comprehensive WES+RNA-seq+ctDNA dataset in BRAF-mutant melanoma to date, 7-year follow-up, K-means-derived three-subtype taxonomy with relative biopsy-site adjustment, and ERBB2 expression as a candidate resistance marker in encorafenib+binimetinib. This is a meaningful extension of prior work rather than a first-in-class discovery.

writing_presentation.justification: The paper is clearly structured with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, with logical flow from individual biomarker subgroup analyses to integrated recursive partitioning. Figures are well described (PFS/OS by TMB, cytolytic score, ERBB2, PI3K mutations; K-means heatmap; ctDNA Kaplan–Meier). Minor issues: methods are dense and some abbreviations are introduced inconsistently (CYT vs cytolytic score), and the Discussion is lengthy with some redundancy on immune biomarker findings. Overall, the writing is publication-ready for a specialist oncology audience.

key_strengths: Largest comprehensive multi-omic biomarker cohort in BRAF V600E/K-mutant melanoma (666 WES, 514 RNA-seq, 336 baseline ctDNA) leveraging a randomized phase III trial with 7-year follow-up
Consistent signal across orthogonal immune readouts (TMB, cytolytic score, PD-L1, IFNγ signature) linking immune contexture to encorafenib+binimetinib benefit
Clinically actionable ctDNA findings: BRAF V600 detectability at baseline prognostic (OS HR 2.3–3.5) and C2D1 clearance associated with improved outcomes
Recursive partitioning integrating LDH, cytolytic score, TMB, ERBB2 provides interpretable survival models
key_concerns: Exploratory retrospective design with pooling of two encorafenib doses (450 mg and 300 mg) across COLUMBUS parts 1 and 2, limiting dose-specific conclusions
No multiplicity correction; all findings explicitly hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation
Unmatched normal controls for WES relying on proxy germline filtering, with potential impact on somatic call quality
Data availability statement and public accession numbers for WES/RNA-seq/ctDNA data not apparent in the text
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality translational analysis of a pivotal phase III trial with robust sample size and multiple orthogonal readouts, placing it at tier 2 (Clinical Cancer Research, JCO PO, Nature Comms-onc) with minor revisions for data sharing and REMARK items.
